question: When did Henrietta Lacks's family learn that her cells were alive in labs around the world?
answer: More than twenty years after she died. In the 1970s researchers contacted the family for blood samples to study the cells, without clearly explaining why. Skloot describes how her children, many unable to afford health insurance, learned that their mother's cells had built careers and an industry, from which they received nothing.
move: Real consent means explaining what will happen, not only asking.
simply: Her family found out decades later, almost by accident, that her cells were famous. Nobody had told them, and they got nothing from it.
why: Asking 'what will this be used for?' before agreeing to give samples or data is your right, and a good habit at any hospital or clinic.
